headline: Historic win: Bangladesh beat Australia in Test for the first time on their soil
summary: The Tigers end a 23-year wait with a dominant nine-wicket victory in Darwin, described by Mark Waugh as one of the biggest upsets in Australian cricket history.
details: Bangladesh achieved a historic nine-wicket victory over Australia in Darwin, marking their first-ever Test win on Australian soil after a 23-year wait.
Former Australian batter Mark Waugh called the result 'potentially the biggest upset I can remember in Australia,' comparing it to the West Indies' win at the Gabba.
The Tigers entered the match as overwhelming underdogs, having been bowled out for just 54 in a tour match against a Cricket Australia XI shortly before the game.
Bangladesh dominated the match, bowling Australia out for 198 on the opening day and scoring 426 in their first innings.
The victory was further highlighted by the team's resilience, as they achieved the win without their top two bowlers, Nahid Rana and Shoriful Islam.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina congratulated the team via video call for their historic achievement in Darwin.
caption:
A 23-year wait is over! 🇧🇩

Bangladesh just secured their first-ever Test win in Australia.

Bangladesh achieved a historic nine-wicket victory over Australia in Darwin, marking their first-ever Test win on Australian soil after a 23-year wait.

Former Australian batter Mark Waugh called the result 'potentially the biggest upset I can remember in Australia,' comparing it to the West Indies' win at the Gabba.

The Tigers entered the match as overwhelming underdogs, having been bowled out for just 54 in a tour match against a Cricket Australia XI shortly before the game.

Bangladesh dominated the match, bowling Australia out for 198 on the opening day and scoring 426 in their first innings.

The victory was further highlighted by the team's resilience, as they achieved the win without their top two bowlers, Nahid Rana and Shoriful Islam.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina congratulated the team via video call for their historic achievement in Darwin.

headline_marked: 7.7 magnitude quake: [[At least 47 killed in Indonesia]]
headline: 7.7 magnitude quake: At least 47 killed in Indonesia
summary: A massive earthquake and dozens of aftershocks struck eastern Indonesia, causing widespread destruction and triggering tsunami warnings.
details: At least 47 people were killed after a magnitude 7.7 earthquake and dozens of aftershocks struck eastern Indonesia, according to the National Disaster Mitigation Agency (BNPB).
Rescue teams have struggled to reach Nagekeo, the region closest to the epicentre, as landslides have blocked roads and disrupted communications.

In the port town of Maumere, rescuers found 20 dead, six injured, and two people trapped under rubble. Governor Emanuel Melkiades Laka Lena reported that at least five people died when buildings collapsed while they slept.
Tsunami waves of less than 1 metre were recorded in several areas, though authorities lifted the tsunami warning about three hours after the early-morning quake.
Preliminary BNPB data shows 157 homes were heavily damaged, while 87 schools, 18 health facilities, and five places of worship were also affected.
Strong shaking was felt across East Nusa Tenggara, West Nusa Tenggara, and parts of South Sulawesi, with some residents reporting tremors lasting about a minute.
Indonesia is located on the "Pacific Ring of Fire," a seismically active zone where tectonic plates meet, making it prone to frequent earthquakes and volcanic eruptions.
caption:
A massive 7.7 magnitude earthquake has left at least 47 dead in eastern Indonesia, with many still trapped under rubble.

At least 47 people were killed after a magnitude 7.7 earthquake and dozens of aftershocks struck eastern Indonesia, according to the National Disaster Mitigation Agency (BNPB).

Rescue teams have struggled to reach Nagekeo, the region closest to the epicentre, as landslides have blocked roads and disrupted communications.

In the port town of Maumere, rescuers found 20 dead, six injured, and two people trapped under rubble. Governor Emanuel Melkiades Laka Lena reported that at least five people died when buildings collapsed while they slept.

Tsunami waves of less than 1 metre were recorded in several areas, though authorities lifted the tsunami warning about three hours after the early-morning quake.

Preliminary BNPB data shows 157 homes were heavily damaged, while 87 schools, 18 health facilities, and five places of worship were also affected.

Strong shaking was felt across East Nusa Tenggara, West Nusa Tenggara, and parts of South Sulawesi, with some residents reporting tremors lasting about a minute.

Indonesia is located on the "Pacific Ring of Fire," a seismically active zone where tectonic plates meet, making it prone to frequent earthquakes and volcanic eruptions.
